newsitem.title: USA: Sonus sees higher oper expenses.
newsitem.headline: Sonus sees higher oper expenses.

text.p: SONUS Pharmaceuticals Inc Thursday said it expects operating expenses to rise in coming quarters as the Company continues to prepare for commercialization of EchoGen.
The rising expenses reflect ongoing and planned clinical trials to study additional indications for EchoGen, as well as higher marketing and administrative expenses.
In a statement, the company said total operating expenses were $4.5 million in the second quarter compared to $3.5 million in the prior-year period.

The company said the increase in operating expenses reflects the continued growth in personnel and the implementation of marketing programs in anticipation of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval and planned product launch of EchoGen.

In addition, revenues in future quarters are partially dependent upon the timing of certain regulatory milestones. As previously announced, the FDA's review of EchoGen has been suspended, awaiting the FDA's response to a court-ordered review of citizen petitions. If the FDA's response is deemed satisfactory by the court, the court's injunction will be lifted, allowing the FDA to continue its review of EchoGen.
SONUS also said it has begun a Phase 3 clinical trial investigating the use of EchoGen as an ultrasound contrast enhancing agent in transrectal ultrasonography of the prostate.
